data-sources-two-kinds.alt: Two columns. Quantitative data are numbers you can count or measure: a count of people in each town, satellite readings of crop cover, phone positions from satellite navigation, shares of homes with internet. Qualitative data are words, pictures and experiences: interviews with farmers, field notes and sketches, photos of a street, travel accounts and news stories. A note says a geographic information system, or GIS, stacks both kinds as layers on one map so you can ask how they line up.
